grades.quote: For any trap (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault) that writes a guest virtual address to `stval` , GVA is set to 1.
grades.reason: Lists the trap types (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, guest-page fault) that write a guest virtual address to stval, and says other traps into HS-mode do not (GVA=0). This is useful but covers only the hypervisor/HS-mode case. It does not give the general S-mode rule or say when stval is zero.
Generic OS textbook discussion of virtual memory and page faults. It is not RISC-V specific and never mentions stval.
Describes Sv57 addressing and says a non-canonical address causes a page fault. It does not mention stval or what value it holds.
A CSR listing table of the virtual supervisor CSRs. It does not describe stval or when it holds a faulting virtual address.
